deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.1 夢 — Vocabulary
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第一章「夢」
notes: Vocabulary for Chapter 1. The opening-page cards (p.5) are checked against the printed page, and the words you wrote in your notebook are tagged flagged_in_notebook. The rest — 三葉's morning, the comet on the news, the twilight lesson in class, braiding cords with her grandmother, and the shrine ritual — is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not copied out page by page, so a few words may turn up a chapter early or late. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: The chapter heading: 第一章「夢」 — Chapter 1, 'Dream'.
cards.context: Careful with the sound change: いち + しょう → いっしょう (small っ), just like 一回 いっかい and 一冊 いっさつ. 第 makes ordinals (第三課 = lesson 3); 章 = chapter (文章, 楽章). The chapters run 第一章 to 第八章 (はっしょう).
cards.example_sentence: 第一章を読み終わるのに一週間かかった。
cards.example_reading: だいいっしょう を よみおわる のに いっしゅうかん かかった。
cards.example_meaning: It took me a week to finish reading Chapter 1.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the very first words: a familiar voice and smell from somewhere long ago.
cards.context: Not just 'nostalgic' — it's the warm ache for something you once knew and have lost. Japanese say 懐かしい! when meeting an old friend or hearing an old song. Kanji 懐 (ふところ, bosom). A feeling of the familiar-but-lost runs through the whole book.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母の家に行くと、いつも懐かしい匂いがする。
cards.example_reading: そぼ の いえ に いく と、 いつも なつかしい におい が する。
cards.example_meaning: Whenever I go to my grandmother's house, there's a smell I know from long ago.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — a remembered voice and scent from a dream.
cards.context: 匂い is a pleasant or neutral smell; 臭い (also read におい, or くさい as an adjective) is a bad smell. 匂いがする = 'there's a smell of…'. Verb: 匂う (におう).
cards.example_sentence: 雨上がりの土の匂いが好きだ。
cards.example_reading: あめあがり の つち の におい が すき だ。
cards.example_meaning: I love the smell of earth after the rain.

meanings: precious (so you want to hold it)
cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 'beloved light and warmth' — the dreamer's sense of being close to someone precious.
cards.context: Full reading is いとおしい — 愛 is read いと here (as in 愛しい いとしい). Softer and more tender than 大切: something so dear you ache to protect it. Literary but common in songs and novels.
cards.example_sentence: 眠っている妹の顔が、なんだか愛おしく思えた。
cards.example_reading: ねむって いる いもうと の かお が、 なんだか いとおしく おもえた。
cards.example_meaning: My little sister's sleeping face suddenly seemed so dear to me.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — light and warmth remembered from the dream.
cards.context: Noun ひかり; verb 光る (ひかる, to shine). On-reading コウ: 日光 (sunlight), 光景 (こうけい, a sight/scene — worth learning next). Light is everywhere in this book: morning sun, twilight, the comet's trail.
cards.example_sentence: 窓から差し込む朝の光で目が覚めた。
cards.example_reading: まど から さしこむ あさ の ひかり で め が さめた。
cards.example_meaning: I woke up to the morning light coming through the window.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 'light and temperature' — here it means the warmth of being close to someone.
cards.context: 温 (warm — 温かい あたたかい) + 度 (degree). In prose, 温度 can mean the warmth of a person, not just a number on a thermometer. Related: 体温 (たいおん, body temperature), 気温 (きおん, air temperature).
cards.example_sentence: 手をつなぐと、相手の温度が伝わってくる。
cards.example_reading: て を つなぐ と、 あいて の おんど が つたわって くる。
cards.example_meaning: When you hold hands, you can feel the other person's warmth.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the dreamer is pressed against someone so closely there's no gap between them (隙間なく).
cards.context: 隙間なく = with no gap at all (see the Nなく grammar card). 隙 alone (すき) = an opening or unguarded moment: 隙がない = no openings. 隙間風 (すきまかぜ) = a draught through a crack.
cards.example_sentence: カーテンの隙間から、細い光がもれていた。
cards.example_reading: カーテン の すきま から、 ほそい ひかり が もれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: A thin line of light was leaking through the gap in the curtains.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — pressed tightly against someone — ぴったりとくっついている.
cards.context: Mimetic word for a perfect, gapless fit. ぴったりくっつく = cling tight; ぴったりのサイズ = a perfect fit; 三時ぴったり = exactly 3:00; あなたにぴったり = perfect for you.
cards.example_sentence: 子猫が母猫にぴったりとくっついて眠っている。
cards.example_reading: こねこ が ははねこ に ぴったり と くっついて ねむって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The kitten is sleeping snuggled right up against its mother.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the dreamer is stuck close to someone important.
cards.context: Intransitive (something sticks); the transitive partner is くっつける (to stick something on). Casually also 'to be all over each other' — いつもくっついている couples or kids.
cards.example_sentence: 寒いので、二人でくっついて座った。
cards.example_reading: さむい ので、 ふたり で くっついて すわった。
cards.example_meaning: It was cold, so the two of us sat huddled together.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the dreamer and that someone are bound together inseparably (分かちがたく).
cards.context: 分かつ (わかつ, literary 'to divide/share') + 〜がたい ('hard to', see the grammar card). Very literary. In the book it's used adverbially: 分かちがたく結びついている.
cards.example_sentence: 二人は、分かちがたい友情で結ばれていた。
cards.example_reading: ふたり は、 わかちがたい ゆうじょう で むすばれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The two of them were bound by an inseparable friendship.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the dreamer is 'tied' to someone — the first hint of the book's big theme.
cards.context: 結ぶ (to tie) + つく (to attach). Abstract use: 努力が結果に結びつく (effort leads to results). Keep an eye on 結ぶ / 結び / ムスビ — tying threads, people and time together becomes one of the story's central ideas.
cards.example_sentence: この町の祭りは、昔から湖と深く結びついている。
cards.example_reading: この まち の まつり は、 むかし から みずうみ と ふかく むすびついて いる。
cards.example_meaning: This town's festival has long been closely tied to the lake.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — like an infant held at the breast — total safety, no fear.
cards.context: Literary/poetic reading ちぶさ (乳 ち = milk, an old word). In medicine it's read にゅうぼう (乳がん = breast cancer). Everyday speech just says 胸 (むね).
cards.example_sentence: 赤ん坊は母親の乳房に顔をうずめて眠った。
cards.example_reading: あかんぼう は ははおや の ちぶさ に かお を うずめて ねむった。
cards.example_meaning: The baby fell asleep with its face buried at its mother's breast.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 乳房に抱かれた — 'held at the breast'; the book reads it いだく here.
cards.context: Same kanji, two readings: だく is the everyday 'hug/hold' (赤ちゃんを抱く). いだく is literary, and it's always いだく for feelings: 夢を抱く (cherish a dream), 不安を抱く (feel uneasy), 疑問を抱く. Passive: 抱かれる.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は、東京への強い憧れを抱いていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は、 とうきょう へ の つよい あこがれ を いだいて いた。
cards.example_meaning: She harboured a strong longing for Tokyo.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the feeling is compared to being a nursing baby, without any loneliness.
cards.context: 乳 (ち, milk) + 飲み (drinking) + 児 (ご, child). More often written 乳飲み子. A literary way of saying a baby still too young for solid food.
cards.example_sentence: 乳飲み児を抱えて働くのは大変だ。
cards.example_reading: ちのみご を かかえて はたらく の は たいへん だ。
cards.example_meaning: Working while caring for a nursing baby is hard.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — no anxiety or loneliness — not even a shred (かけらもない).
cards.context: Kanji: 欠片 (欠ける = to chip + 片 = piece), but often written in hiragana. Literal: ガラスのかけら (a glass shard). With a negative: 〜のかけらもない = not a trace of (see grammar card). Fragments become important later in the story.
cards.example_sentence: 割れたコップのかけらで指を切った。
cards.example_reading: われた コップ の かけら で ゆび を きった。
cards.example_meaning: I cut my finger on a shard of the broken glass.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — in the dream, nothing has been lost yet (失ったもの).
cards.context: Weightier and more literary than なくす: used for losing people, memories, chances, confidence. 気を失う = to faint. 失ったもの (what was lost) — loss and searching for it is the heart of this book.
cards.example_sentence: 事故で記憶を失った人の話を読んだ。
cards.example_reading: じこ で きおく を うしなった ひと の はなし を よんだ。
cards.example_meaning: I read a story about someone who lost their memory in an accident.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — 未だひとつもなく — not a single thing lost yet.
cards.context: Literary まだ, almost always paired with a negative: 未だ〜ない = still not. 未だに (いまだに) = even now, still. 未 = 'not yet' (未来 = the future, lit. 'not yet come').
cards.example_sentence: 彼からの返事は、未だに来ない。
cards.example_reading: かれ から の へんじ は、 いまだに こない。
cards.example_meaning: There's still no reply from him.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — a very sweet feeling (甘やかな気持ち) filling the body.
cards.context: な-adjective: 甘やかな気持ち / 甘やかな香り. Poetic, soft. Don't confuse it with 甘やかす (あまやかす, to spoil/pamper a child) — same root, different word.
cards.example_sentence: 花の甘やかな香りが部屋に広がった。
cards.example_reading: はな の あまやかな かおり が へや に ひろがった。
cards.example_meaning: The sweet scent of the flowers spread through the room.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the sweet feeling fills the body with a warm tingle (じんじんと).
cards.context: Physical: 足がじんじんする (pins and needles; a dull throb after cold or a knock). Here it's emotional — a feeling that spreads and pulses. Compare ずきずき (sharp throbbing pain) and ひりひり (stinging).
cards.example_sentence: 雪の中を歩いたので、指先がじんじんする。
cards.example_reading: ゆき の なか を あるいた ので、 ゆびさき が じんじん する。
cards.example_meaning: I walked through the snow, so my fingertips are tingling.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — a sweet feeling fills the body (体に満ちている).
cards.context: 〜に満ちる / 〜に満ちている = to be full of: 希望に満ちた顔 (a face full of hope). Also 月が満ちる (the moon waxes), 潮が満ちる (the tide comes in). Transitive: 満たす (みたす).
cards.example_sentence: 春の森は、鳥の声に満ちていた。
cards.example_reading: はる の もり は、 とり の こえ に みちて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The spring forest was full of birdsong.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — ふと、目が開く — the dreamer's eyes suddenly open.
cards.context: Something happens by itself, with no intention: ふと思い出す (it suddenly comes to mind), ふと目が覚める, ふと見ると (glancing up, I saw…). Quieter than 突然 (dramatically sudden). Extremely common in novels.
cards.example_sentence: 駅のホームで、ふと昔の友だちの顔を思い出した。
cards.example_reading: えき の ホーム で、 ふと むかし の ともだち の かお を おもいだした。
cards.example_meaning: On the station platform, an old friend's face suddenly came to mind.

meanings: to wake up and open one's eyes
cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the dream ends: ふと、目が開く。
cards.context: The book reads 開く as ひらく here; めがあく is also correct. ひらく suggests opening outward or wide — also 花が開く (flowers bloom), 会を開く (hold a meeting). Transitive with を: 目を開ける (あける).
cards.example_sentence: 名前を呼ばれて、ゆっくりと目が開いた。
cards.example_reading: なまえ を よばれて、 ゆっくり と め が ひらいた。
cards.example_meaning: Someone called my name, and my eyes slowly opened.

cards.scene: Opening page (p.5) — the first thing seen on waking: 天井。
cards.context: Irregular reading: 井 is normally い (井戸 いど, well) or セイ, but here it's ジョウ. 天 (heaven/sky) + 井. 天井が高い = high-ceilinged. Waking-up scenes come back again and again in this story.
cards.example_sentence: ベッドに横になって、ぼんやり天井を見つめた。
cards.example_reading: ベッド に よこ に なって、 ぼんやり てんじょう を みつめた。
cards.example_meaning: I lay on the bed and stared blankly at the ceiling.

cards.scene: Useful for the morning scenes in 三葉's house — and for her friends' comments about how messy she looked the day before.
cards.context: 寝 (sleep) + 癖 (habit; a kink or curl). 寝癖がつく = to get bedhead; 寝癖を直す = to fix it. 癖 alone (くせ) = a habit: 口癖 (くちぐせ) = a pet phrase.
cards.example_sentence: 寝癖がひどくて、帽子をかぶって学校に行った。
cards.example_reading: ねぐせ が ひどくて、 ぼうし を かぶって がっこう に いった。
cards.example_meaning: My bedhead was so bad I wore a hat to school.

cards.scene: 三葉's father is the mayor of 糸守町 — and she can't escape it at school.
cards.context: 町 (town) + 長 (head). Compare 市長 (city mayor), 村長 (village head), 社長 (company president). Fun clash: ちょうちょう is also 蝶々 (butterfly).
cards.example_sentence: 新しい町長は、駅前の再開発を約束した。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい ちょうちょう は、 えきまえ の さいかいはつ を やくそく した。
cards.example_meaning: The new mayor promised to redevelop the area in front of the station.

cards.scene: Her father is campaigning in the mayoral election — posters, speeches, and awkward moments for 三葉.
cards.context: 選 (choose) + 挙 (raise up). 選挙運動 = election campaign; 選挙カー = a campaign van blasting a candidate's name from loudspeakers, a very Japanese sight; 立候補 (りっこうほ) = to run for office.
cards.example_sentence: 町長選挙が近づき、町中にポスターが貼られた。
cards.example_reading: ちょうちょうせんきょ が ちかづき、 まちじゅう に ポスター が はられた。
cards.example_meaning: With the mayoral election coming up, posters went up all over town.

cards.scene: The mayor's campaign speech in town, which 三葉 would rather not be seen near.
cards.context: 演説する = to make a speech, especially a political one. 街頭演説 (がいとうえんぜつ) = street-corner speech. スピーチ is the lighter word (weddings, school).
cards.example_sentence: 駅前で候補者が演説をしていた。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ で こうほしゃ が えんぜつ を して いた。
cards.example_meaning: A candidate was making a speech in front of the station.

cards.scene: テッシー's family runs the local construction company — a big deal in a small town.
cards.context: 土木 (civil engineering) + 建築 (building) + 屋 (trade/shop). Slightly blunt and colloquial; the neutral term is 建設会社 (けんせつがいしゃ). In small towns the builder and the town office are often closely tied.
cards.example_sentence: 叔父は田舎で小さな土建屋をやっている。
cards.example_reading: おじ は いなか で ちいさな どけんや を やって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My uncle runs a small construction firm out in the countryside.

cards.scene: 三葉 has to put up with classmates sniping about her family behind her back.
cards.context: 陰 (shadow) + 口 (mouth). 陰口を言う / 陰口をたたく = to badmouth someone behind their back. 悪口 (わるぐち) is any insult; 陰口 is specifically said where the person can't hear — or is meant to overhear.
cards.example_sentence: 陰口を言う人とは、あまり付き合いたくない。
cards.example_reading: かげぐち を いう ひと と は、 あまり つきあいたくない。
cards.example_meaning: I don't really want to hang around people who talk behind others' backs.

cards.scene: The news is full of a comet (ティアマト彗星) about to pass close to Earth.
cards.context: 彗 (broom — a comet looks like a sweeping broom) + 星. Compare 流れ星 (shooting star), 隕石 (meteorite), 惑星 (planet). The comet is the story's ticking clock — expect it in every chapter.
cards.example_sentence: 千年に一度の彗星を見るために、多くの人が山に登った。
cards.example_reading: せんねん に いちど の すいせい を みる ため に、 おおく の ひと が やま に のぼった。
cards.example_meaning: Lots of people climbed the mountain to see the once-in-a-thousand-years comet.

cards.scene: The comet only comes round once in a very long cycle — the news makes a big deal of it.
cards.context: 周 (around) + 期 (period). 周期的 = periodic; 公転周期 (こうてんしゅうき) = orbital period. Also everyday: 生活の周期 (the rhythm of daily life).
cards.example_sentence: この彗星は、約七十六年の周期で地球に近づく。
cards.example_reading: この すいせい は、 やく ななじゅうろくねん の しゅうき で ちきゅう に ちかづく。
cards.example_meaning: This comet approaches Earth on a cycle of about 76 years.

cards.scene: News reports count down the comet's approach to Earth.
cards.context: 接近する = to approach. News phrase: 最接近 (さいせっきん) = closest approach. Also used for storms: 台風が接近する (a typhoon is approaching).
cards.example_sentence: 台風の接近で、明日の授業は休みになった。
cards.example_reading: たいふう の せっきん で、 あした の じゅぎょう は やすみ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Classes were cancelled tomorrow because of the approaching typhoon.

cards.scene: The comet will be visible to the naked eye — no telescope needed.
cards.context: 肉 (flesh) + 眼 (eye). 肉眼で見える = visible to the naked eye. Opposite: 望遠鏡 (ぼうえんきょう, telescope).
cards.example_sentence: 今夜は、肉眼でも土星が見えるらしい。
cards.example_reading: こんや は、 にくがん で も どせい が みえる らしい。
cards.example_meaning: Apparently you can see Saturn with the naked eye tonight.

cards.scene: 三葉's classical-literature class, where the teacher explains old words for twilight.
cards.context: At Japanese high schools 古典 means classical Japanese and Chinese texts (古文 + 漢文). Also 'a classic' in general: 古典的 = classic(al). This one lesson plants several of the book's key words.
cards.example_sentence: 古典の授業で、千年以上前の和歌を読んだ。
cards.example_reading: こてん の じゅぎょう で、 せんねん いじょう まえ の わか を よんだ。
cards.example_meaning: In classical literature class we read poems from over a thousand years ago.

meanings: the Man'yōshū (oldest anthology of Japanese poetry)
cards.scene: The teacher's example of the old word for twilight comes from a 万葉集 poem.
cards.context: About 4,500 poems compiled in the 8th century. 万 (ten thousand) + 葉 (leaves = words) + 集 (collection). Notice 葉 — the same kanji as in 三葉 and 四葉.
cards.example_sentence: 万葉集には、身分を問わずさまざまな人の歌が収められている。
cards.example_reading: まんようしゅう に は、 みぶん を とわず さまざまな ひと の うた が おさめられて いる。
cards.example_meaning: The Man'yōshū contains poems by all kinds of people, regardless of rank.

cards.scene: The twilight lesson in class: dusk is when you can't quite make out who someone is.
cards.context: 黄昏 (たそがれ) is a 熟字訓 — a special reading of the whole word that you can't get from the separate kanji. It comes from 誰そ彼 ('who is that?'). Also figurative: 人生の黄昏 (the twilight of life). Twilight matters enormously later.
cards.example_sentence: 黄昏時の空は、オレンジから紫へと色を変えた。
cards.example_reading: たそがれどき の そら は、 オレンジ から むらさき へ と いろ を かえた。
cards.example_meaning: The twilight sky changed from orange to purple.

cards.scene: The teacher writes this old phrase to show where the word for twilight comes from.
cards.context: Classical Japanese: 誰 (た, who) + そ (emphatic particle, like modern ぞ) + 彼 (かれ, that person) → 'Who is that?' At dusk you can't tell faces apart, so you have to ask. It later softened into たそがれ.
cards.example_sentence: 「誰そ彼」は、夕暮れに人の顔が見えにくいことから生まれた言葉だ。
cards.example_reading: 「たそかれ」 は、 ゆうぐれ に ひと の かお が みえにくい こと から うまれた ことば だ。
cards.example_meaning: 'Tasokare' is a word born from how hard it is to see people's faces at dusk.

cards.scene: The classical twin of 誰そ彼 — worth knowing next to the twilight words from 三葉's class.
cards.context: 彼 (か, that) + は + 誰 (たれ, who) → 'Who is that?' — the same question, asked at dawn. Classical poets used かはたれ for morning twilight and たそかれ for evening.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は誰時の薄暗い道を、新聞配達の自転車が走っていく。
cards.example_reading: かはたれどき の うすぐらい みち を、 しんぶんはいたつ の じてんしゃ が はしって いく。
cards.example_meaning: A newspaper delivery bike rides down the dim road in the half-light before dawn.

cards.scene: Root of the town's own word for twilight (かたわれ時) — and a word the whole story leans on.
cards.context: 片 (one side) + 割れ (split). Three senses, and the book plays on all of them: one of a matched pair (a lost glove's 片割れ), a fragment of something broken, and someone's 'other half'.
cards.example_sentence: 片方の手袋をなくして、残った片割れだけが引き出しにある。
cards.example_reading: かたほう の てぶくろ を なくして、 のこった かたわれ だけ が ひきだし に ある。
cards.example_meaning: I lost one glove, and only its partner is left in the drawer.

cards.scene: In class it comes up that in Itomori's local speech, twilight is called かたわれ時.
cards.context: The town's own word for dusk, from 片割れ (one half of a pair) + 時. A hint that at twilight, two halves might meet. Remember it — it matters a great deal later in the book.
cards.example_sentence: かたわれ時になると、湖の色が少しずつ変わっていく。
cards.example_reading: かたわれどき に なる と、 みずうみ の いろ が すこし ずつ かわって いく。
cards.example_meaning: At twilight, the colour of the lake gradually changes.

cards.scene: With no café in town, 三葉 and her friends hang out on a bench by a vending machine instead.
cards.context: Short for 自動販売機 (じどうはんばいき, 'automatic selling machine'). Japan has one on almost every corner — even deep in the countryside.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前の自販機で、温かいお茶を買った。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ の じはんき で、 あたたかい おちゃ を かった。
cards.example_meaning: I bought hot tea from the vending machine in front of the station.

cards.scene: 三葉 is fed up with her small mountain town and dreams of the big city.
cards.context: Irregular reading (熟字訓): 田 + 舎 → いなか. Can sound negative (田舎くさい = countrified) or warm (田舎に帰る = go back to one's hometown). The country-vs-Tokyo contrast drives the early chapters.
cards.example_sentence: 田舎の夜は、星がよく見えて静かだ。
cards.example_reading: いなか の よる は、 ほし が よく みえて しずか だ。
cards.example_meaning: Nights in the countryside are quiet, and you can see the stars well.

cards.scene: 三葉, 四葉 and their grandmother make braided cords by hand — a family tradition of the shrine.
cards.context: 組む (to braid, put together) + 紐 (ひも, cord/string). Made on a wooden braiding stand. 三葉 ties her hair with one. Arguably the most important object in the story — notice every time it appears.
cards.example_sentence: おばあちゃんに習って、初めて組紐を編んだ。
cards.example_reading: おばあちゃん に ならって、 はじめて くみひも を あんだ。
cards.example_meaning: I learned from my grandma and braided a cord for the first time.

cards.scene: Braiding the cords with grandmother.
cards.context: セーターを編む (knit a sweater), 髪を編む (braid hair → 三つ編み みつあみ = a braid), 本を編む (edit/compile a book). Noun: 編み物 (あみもの, knitting).
cards.example_sentence: 冬になると、母は毎年マフラーを編んでくれた。
cards.example_reading: ふゆ に なる と、 はは は まいとし マフラー を あんで くれた。
cards.example_meaning: Every winter, my mother would knit me a scarf.

cards.scene: Grandmother tells of a great fire long ago that burned the town's old records — so the meaning of the rituals was lost and only their form remains.
cards.context: Read たいか, not おおび. Old town fires are often named after where they started (〜の大火). 火事 (かじ) is the everyday word for a house fire.
cards.example_sentence: 江戸時代の大火で、町の半分が焼けてしまった。
cards.example_reading: えどじだい の たいか で、 まち の はんぶん が やけて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Half the town burned down in a great fire during the Edo period.

cards.scene: The shrine's autumn festival — the night of the ritual dance — is a harvest festival.
cards.context: 豊 (abundant) + 穣 (ripe grain). 豊穣祭 = harvest festival; 五穀豊穣 (ごこくほうじょう) = 'a rich harvest of the five grains', a standard prayer at shrines. Everyday word: 豊作 (ほうさく).
cards.example_sentence: 村の人々は、神社で五穀豊穣を祈った。
cards.example_reading: むら の ひとびと は、 じんじゃ で ごこくほうじょう を いのった。
cards.example_meaning: The villagers prayed at the shrine for a bountiful harvest.

cards.scene: The gate marking the shrine's sacred ground, where the festival takes place.
cards.context: Passing through a 鳥居 means entering the god's space. 鳥 (bird) + 居 (to be/stay) — a 'bird perch'. 鳥居をくぐる = to pass under a torii.
cards.example_sentence: 赤い鳥居をくぐると、空気が変わった気がした。
cards.example_reading: あかい とりい を くぐる と、 くうき が かわった き が した。
cards.example_meaning: When I passed under the red torii, the air seemed to change.

cards.scene: The shrine grounds during the festival.
cards.context: Tricky reading: 内 is だい here (not ない). Means everything inside the shrine's boundary. 境内で遊ぶ = to play on the shrine grounds.
cards.example_sentence: 夏祭りの日、神社の境内には屋台が並んだ。
cards.example_reading: なつまつり の ひ、 じんじゃ の けいだい に は やたい が ならんだ。
cards.example_meaning: On the day of the summer festival, food stalls lined the shrine grounds.

cards.scene: 三葉 and 四葉 serve as shrine maidens at their family's shrine.
cards.context: Special reading — the kanji 巫 (フ) and 女 (ジョ) won't get you みこ. 巫女さん dance in rituals, help the priest and sell charms. White top, red hakama.
cards.example_sentence: 正月になると、神社の巫女さんたちはとても忙しい。
cards.example_reading: しょうがつ に なる と、 じんじゃ の みこ さん たち は とても いそがしい。
cards.example_meaning: At New Year, the shrine maidens are extremely busy.

cards.scene: The sisters perform a ritual dance at the festival in front of the townspeople.
cards.context: 舞 is slow, graceful, often sacred dance; verb 舞う (まう) — also 'to flutter': 花びらが舞う, 雪が舞う. 踊り (おどり) is livelier, more everyday dancing. 舞を舞う = to perform a dance.
cards.example_sentence: 祭りの夜、二人の巫女が神様のために舞を舞った。
cards.example_reading: まつり の よる、 ふたり の みこ が かみさま の ため に まい を まった。
cards.example_meaning: On the night of the festival, two shrine maidens danced for the god.

cards.scene: The dance and the sake are offerings dedicated to the god.
cards.context: 奉 (offer up respectfully) + 納 (deliver). 奉納する: dedicating sake, dances, plaques (絵馬) or performances to a shrine's god. 奉納の舞 = a dance offered to the god.
cards.example_sentence: 秋祭りでは、地元の子どもたちが太鼓を奉納する。
cards.example_reading: あきまつり で は、 じもと の こども たち が たいこ を ほうのう する。
cards.example_meaning: At the autumn festival, the local kids perform drumming as an offering.

cards.scene: As part of the ritual, the shrine maidens chew rice and spit it into a small vessel to make sake — mortifying for 三葉 in front of her classmates.
cards.context: 口 + 噛み (chew) + 酒 (さけ → ざけ). One of the oldest ways to make sake: enzymes in saliva start the fermentation. This little vessel of sake matters hugely later on.
cards.example_sentence: 昔の日本では、口噛み酒を神様に供えていたという。
cards.example_reading: むかし の にほん で は、 くちかみざけ を かみさま に そなえて いた と いう。
cards.example_meaning: They say that in ancient Japan, mouth-chewed sake was offered to the gods.

cards.scene: Chewing the rice for the ritual sake.
cards.context: ガムを噛む (chew gum), 犬に噛まれる (get bitten by a dog), 舌を噛む (bite your tongue). Slang: 噛んだ! = 'I fluffed my line!'
cards.example_sentence: よく噛んで食べなさいと、祖母によく言われた。
cards.example_reading: よく かんで たべなさい と、 そぼ に よく いわれた。
cards.example_meaning: My grandmother always told me to chew my food well.

cards.scene: How 口噛み酒 works: the chewed rice ferments into sake.
cards.context: 発 (start) + 酵 (ferment). 発酵する / 発酵させる. 発酵食品 = fermented foods (味噌, 納豆, 漬物).
cards.example_sentence: 納豆は、大豆を発酵させて作る。
cards.example_reading: なっとう は、 だいず を はっこう させて つくる。
cards.example_meaning: Natto is made by fermenting soybeans.

cards.scene: The long stone steps of the shrine, where 三葉 lets out her frustration.
cards.context: 石 (stone) + 段 (step). Shrines often sit at the top of a long flight of 石段. 階段 is the general word for stairs.
cards.example_sentence: 神社まで、百段以上の石段を上った。
cards.example_reading: じんじゃ まで、 ひゃくだん いじょう の いしだん を のぼった。
cards.example_meaning: I climbed more than a hundred stone steps to reach the shrine.

cards.scene: Fed up, 三葉 shouts a wish about who she wants to be in her next life.
cards.context: The set: 前世 (ぜんせ, past life), 現世 (げんせ, this life), 来世 (next life). 来世は〜に生まれたい = 'In my next life I want to be born as…'. Be careful what you wish for in this story.
cards.example_sentence: 来世は鳥に生まれて、自由に空を飛びたい。
cards.example_reading: らいせ は とり に うまれて、 じゆう に そら を とびたい。
cards.example_meaning: In my next life I want to be born a bird and fly freely through the sky.

cards.scene: 三葉's wish involves becoming a handsome boy in Tokyo.
cards.context: Slang: イケてる (cool) + メン (men, and a pun on 面 'face'). Very common in everyday speech and the media. The female equivalent is often 美人 or (slangy) 美女.
cards.example_sentence: 新しく来た先生がイケメンだと、クラスで話題になった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしく きた せんせい が イケメン だ と、 クラス で わだい に なった。
cards.example_meaning: The whole class was talking about how good-looking the new teacher was.

cards.scene: On the cover: ちーこ・挿絵 — illustrations by ちーこ (and 新海誠・作 = written by 新海誠).
cards.context: 挿 (to insert, as in 挿す) + 絵 (picture) → pictures slotted into a text. The credit line pattern is Name・作 (author) and Name・挿絵 (illustrator). イラスト is the everyday word.
cards.example_sentence: この本には、かわいい挿絵がたくさん入っている。
cards.example_reading: この ほん に は、 かわいい さしえ が たくさん はいって いる。
cards.example_meaning: This book has lots of cute illustrations in it.

cards.scene: On the cover: 角川つばさ文庫 — the Kadokawa Tsubasa paperback imprint for young readers.
cards.context: 文庫本 = a small, cheap paperback (A6 size). Publishers name their paperback lines 〜文庫. つばさ文庫 editions add furigana and illustrations for younger readers — the same story as the adult novel.
cards.example_sentence: 電車で読むなら、軽い文庫本がいちばんだ。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ で よむ なら、 かるい ぶんこぼん が いちばん だ。
cards.example_meaning: If you're reading on the train, a light paperback is best.
